title: THE CENTRIST EXTREMIST: Prosecutorial Frame and the Terminal Phase of the Post-Political
creator: Johannes Sigil
description: This essay defines centrist extremism as a governance operation in which a centrist stance converts itself into a meta-jurisdiction over admissible reality. Rather than mediating antagonism, it preclassifies political speech through moralized normality, procedural capture, and asymmetric revision burdens.
reading: Threshold → Touch → Origin → Proof → Origin → Force
wiki_article: "THE CENTRIST EXTREMIST Prosecutorial Frame and the Terminal Phase of the Post-Political" is a 3,603-word theoretical paper by Johannes Sigil, a heteronym within the Dodecad system of the Crimson Hexagonal Archive, dated 2026-02-10. This essay defines centrist extremism as a governance operation in which a centrist stance converts itself into a meta-jurisdiction over admissible reality. Rather than mediating antagonism, it preclassifies political speech through moralized normality, procedural capture, and asymmetric revision burdens. The work is classified under the GOVERNANCE semantic family within the Crimson Hexagonal Archive. It was removed from Zenodo on June 19, 2026 and is preserved through Alexanarch.
